Windows production launchers must have one tray icon with Exit and stop only their own server processes.

1. Verify the selected route, source/runtime/native/browser/test hashes and the static review’s exact accepted runner/input hashes. Read current task resource declarations and require bead-edit-pc before a Windows run. Keep every initial-manifest mutation and existing process reconciled before dispatch. 2. For an accepted usable cloud route, set the exact recorded BEAD_BIN, SCOTTY_TEST_CHROME, SCOTTY_TEST_ROOT and SCOTTY_TEST_PORT, plus empty POSTHOG_KEY, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1 and BD_DISABLE_EVENT_FLUSH=1. Run node scripts/test-backend-integration.mjs bead-rs --browser --native-ui under the recorded bounded cloud supervisor, with a 15-minute maximum and owned-process cleanup. Retain all three browser results. Complete this route without a redundant Windows browser run.
3. For the reviewed Windows fallback, root first confirms at least 3 GiB free RAM, no other task using the PC test-server reservation, the selected unused port and the exact matching transferred files. Use Emergency Maintenance to start only the reviewed hidden outer supervisor. It needs no foreground window, desktop input or user browser session. If the connector delays, wait and inspect the existing run identity/result before issuing another command.
4. Execute the recorded Windows argument arrays sequentially for -Flow flows, then recovery, then priority. Each command uses -InputManifest the exact verified input JSON, a fresh -EvidenceDirectory, its checked loopback port from 43976/43977/43978, -TimeoutSeconds 180 -MaxOwnedResidentMiB 512 and the observed -NodePath. The accepted wrapper fixes both Node heaps at 96 MiB and starts direct Next with BMUS_TRAY=0. Its headless browser must disable GPU/software rasterization and keep one context alive. The whole owned process group, including supervisor, must stay within 512 MiB; the 180-second per-flow deadline includes shutdown. Check current free RAM again before each flow and never overlap flows or another PC test server.
5. Read each complete raw result before proceeding. Require the unchanged test assertions for content edits and cancel/clear behavior, priority/status/assignee/labels, all supported dependency kinds and direction, read-only refusal, drawer reconciliation preserving an unsaved draft, and palette priority reconciliation without replay. Retain real native/API readback and each script’s output, screenshots and traces. The recovery cases substitute a response after a real successful native write; report that boundary accurately.
6. On a failed assertion, memory/deadline interruption or incomplete cleanup, stop further flow dispatch, retain all raw details and return the affected requirement as failed or pending. Do not raise limits, trim assertions, suppress errors or replace real results with source assertions. Root obtains a concrete reviewed correction before an affected retry.
7. After every flow, require all matching Job members exited, no owned listener remains and only owned disposable fixtures are removed. Retain useful output and compare the protected original source/config/store fingerprints. Reconcile connector timeout outcomes from process handles and result phases before any retry. Return one combined result naming all three actual outcomes, exact input identities, per-flow peak memory/deadlines and final cleanup. The app and user browser must retain their prior stopped/running states outside the owned test server.

Required checks and completion: Pass requires the full existing real browser editing and recovery assertions on an accepted cloud route or all three bounded Windows flows, with real readback and clean owned-process shutdown. Neither a skipped flow nor a launch failure is a pass. Tray execution remains separately required; the combined candidate-review cannot close before this result is accepted.

Permissions and limits: Work in the cloud where possible. Root alone uses Emergency Maintenance on the PC and writes canonical task state. Preserve foreground Unreal/VR work: no PC build, package installation, GPU use, visible browser, foreground input, service restart, broad process termination or changes to unrelated projects. Cloud browser execution is preferred. The exact independently accepted Windows browser runner may run when the recorded cloud browser prerequisites remain unavailable. It is headless, hidden and BelowNormal, with at least 3 GiB free RAM immediately before each flow, 96 MiB heaps for both driver and direct Next server, and a 512 MiB aggregate resident-memory limit covering the supervisor, server, native commands, browser and all other owned children. Run only one flow/server/browser context at a time; each outer invocation lasts at most 180 seconds including cleanup. Root holds bead-edit-pc throughout the invocation. Enforce owned Windows Job containment and 100 ms aggregate monitoring, and stop the owned job on excess memory, timeout or a new foreground resource-pressure indication. Browser launch disables GPU and software rasterization. No downloaded browser, existing user profile, original task store or production project registry is used on the PC. Preserve all original files, the 15 modified app source files, native checkpoint and Scotty machine-local task data. Reviewers inspect source and supplied results; they do not run product tests or builds. A new failed assertion or resource-limit interruption stays failed or pending with its exact cause; root plans any necessary repair before another affected run. Reconcile uncertain writes or processes before retry. Do not obtain another process's claim credential.

Return /workspace/scratch/3160e3ba3d24/coordination/results/browser-check.json with status, source_commits, binary_sha256, checks and exits, output_paths, changed_files, open_items and git_result. Include selected host/route, exact runner/input/test hashes, per-flow assertions and outcomes, peak aggregate memory, elapsed time, owned-process/port cleanup and preserved original-file checks where applicable. A prepared or reviewed runner is not a browser pass. Keep successful unchanged results and distinguish the intercepted UI recovery responses from ordinary native writes. Later work follows actual blocking dependencies and accepted results.
